chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: "Grooving" credits and R. I. O'Nan
summary: McRae finished a pencil sketch by trumpeter Frank Brown and another writer; they listen to the recording.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: were better for him to play, and the band was backing him better, and everything like that. And it shows in 'Grooving,' was one of the things we -- things were quite a hit with the band. We used this arrangement a lot on the show. It was a show tune. We used to open with this a lot. And it went over real big, because Louie was spotted -- was different -- and it showed him off much better.
The recording liner notes credit you, Frank Brown and R.I. O'Nan as the co-composers of this.
He was one of the writers from Florida. I think he's a boy out of Florida. Jessie Brown, trumpet player -- you see his name on there?
Frank Brown. Well we call him Jessie Brown. Frank Brown and the other writer. I never met him. They had this thing

together and I finished it up when he came in the band.
He had like a pencil copy of it, you know. And I wrote it up. It was published by Louis Music later. Had just an orchestration out on it.
Yeah, you can see right in there how we changed it around, you know.--instead of him just blowing all the way through the arrangements.
